EIGHTEENTH RECORD IN THIS FILE'S SERIES, AND THE FIRST THIS BRANCH HAS TAKEN FOR A COMMIT THAT IS NEITHER A MERGE NOR A REBASE - a lint-cleaning commit over four files under `scripts/`, which is why only ONE tree moves. WHY THAT MOVES THE STAMP AT ALL: `renderer-driver.mjs` and this branch's own three scripts files (`new-chat-shortcut.test.mjs`, `new-chat-shortcut-evidence.tsx`, `new-chat-shortcut-evidence.vite.mjs`) are exactly the files `pnpm lint:scripts` charges this change for, and the ratchet fails any file a change touches that is not lint-clean, so all four were cleaned in one pass: the formatter and the fixable rules by `biome check --write`, the rest by hand - regex literals hoisted to module constants (none carries `g` or `y`, so none carries a `lastIndex` from one use to the next, and two of the five were asked in more than one scene), the driver's two `delete env.<KEY>` sites written as `env.<KEY> = undefined` (Node omits an `undefined` env value from a child exactly as a removal does - measured on 22.22.0 and 24.18.1 - and the app's own gate takes only `1`/`true` and reports anything else as a TYPO, so neither form could arm an unarmed launch), and `previous !== null && previous.equals(bytes)` written as `previous?.equals(bytes)`, which answers identically for the `null` and Buffer states that variable holds. NONE OF IT IS A PIXEL: no frame was re-taken and no sweep was run, so `frames` 3029, `surfaces` 363, `themes` 12, `capturedAt`, `captureOrigin` and `head` are untouched, `srcTree` does not move at all because this commit touches nothing under `src/`, and only `scriptsTree` is re-derived from the tree it is committed in. ONE ASSERTION IN THAT PASS WAS REPAIRED RATHER THAN REFORMATTED, which is why this is a fix and not only a style commit: `new-chat-shortcut.test.mjs`'s canvas pin carried an empty character class (`[]`), which matches nothing, so the check that the canvas holds no role list of its own could never fail - it now reads a quoted `[role=` selector and is proved against the five shapes a violating call can take, and against the attribute-constant and prose cases this pin is deliberately not about.

Re-measured, `performance.now()` reads 119.674 ms against a 120 ms budget and 599.296 ms against 600 ms, the same sub-millisecond early fire QA saw at 599.25 ms, so the comment now names the early fire and rests the remedy on it. The ceiling's headroom is restated in the same pass as 12-18x (34 ms worst overshoot over 300 runs at this site, 22 ms in QA's sweep) rather than the 26x a 15-run sample suggested.
